public_rationale: The planning experiment shows that a system using formal representations and a classical solver can outperform direct LLM planning. It does not establish which addition causes the improvement. Architectural absence and poor performance together are insufficient to prove the causal phrase to their peril.
limitations: The cited experiment concerns planning rather than the full range of LLM failures.
A beneficial combined intervention does not isolate the contribution of each component.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs try to function without classical world models, and this harms them.

statement.excerpt: LLMs try — to their peril — to live without classical world models.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

our_interpretation: Classical world models means explicit entity-and-state representations with defined update procedures, following the post's examples.
The target is standard LLMs discussed at publication, rather than complete applications equipped with external databases, simulators, or planners.
To their peril asserts that the absence causes performance failures; it does not specify that every failure has this cause.
Learned internal representations are not automatically classical world models.
criteria.support_condition: Architectural evidence establishes the relevant absence, and controlled comparisons show that adding an explicit world model reduces failures while holding other material capabilities constant.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant models already contain classical world models, or well-controlled tests reject the proposed causal mechanism across the claimed scope.

evidence.explanation: The hybrid improves planning, but it combines formal problem descriptions with an external search algorithm. That bundled comparison does not identify the absence of a world model as the cause of the baseline failures.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled comparisons that vary explicit state representation while matching search, computation, training, and feedback, followed by replication across relevant tasks and models.
